full_narration: While he sorts tools, why can one nearby yawn make his mouth copy it? He grabs the worn book, and the answer opens. Your eyes catch the stretching jaw. Your brain recognizes a familiar human action. Attention locks onto it. Perception and motor systems may prime a matching response. The exact mechanism remains unsettled. Scientists call it contagious yawning. It occurs in humans and some social animals. Social connection may influence it. But evidence linking it directly to empathy is mixed. So seeing a yawn can make your own easier to trigger. One yawn can quietly set another in motion. Like and subscribe to grow more questions.
